entries.reason: Open-ended JSON-compatible values need one Protobuf representation that retains distinct Int64 and Double values across typed domain snapshots.
entries.schema: eve.persistence.proto.DynamicValue is a recursive oneof for null, bool, Int64, finite Double, string, list and object.
entries.version: The shared value message is embedded inside versioned owning-domain messages; it is not an independent persistent root.
entries.migration: Owning domains migrate their outer schema and can convert prior JSON values through the same dynamic runtime contract.
entries.unknown_fields: Owning-domain binary restore rejects unknown fields recursively; the codec rejects unset kinds, false null markers, duplicate object keys and non-finite doubles.
entries.restore_atomicity: Decode builds an independent Value; encode swaps a complete temporary message only after every nested value succeeds.

entries.reason: Foundation persistence modules share a typed conversion boundary for genuinely dynamic data.

trim.absent_profile: No L1-L4 trim claim is made for the common codec.

entries.thread_affinity: The caller owns the input and output values; conversion has no shared state or callbacks.
cost_notes: Encoding and decoding cost linear time in recursively owned value size per persistence operation.

entries.reason: Release and assertion-enabled consumers share the same observation and move bookkeeping; only diagnostic checks are conditional.
evidence: docs/dev/Result检查与不得丢弃返回值规范.md
protocol: Native owning Result values retain their public signatures and two-byte observation layout across assertion policies. Observation and move duty updates are identical; moved-from sources are disarmed in both policies. No persistent schema or ECS data is introduced.
entries.thread_affinity: One owner observes or mutates a Result at a time; cross-thread handoff requires synchronization. No callbacks or provider lookup.

trim.evidence: Two translation units deliberately use different assertion policies; the same interop executable is linked to OBJECT and SHARED profile checks. Both module consumers rebuild the inline contract.

cost_notes.why: Constant-size flag updates per value operation; Release removes assertion checks, not bookkeeping. No allocation or expensive preparation API.

entries.reason: Structured result status preserves immutable diagnostics while successful values do not allocate commit-phase workspace.
evidence: docs/dev/Result检查与不得丢弃返回值规范.md
protocol: Native by-value Status/Result foundation; no ECS/Link, capabilities, events, script binding class or tool protocol is introduced. Existing projections serialize the same status codes and diagnostic order. No persistent schema changes.

Successful Status contains no diagnostics container; copying/moving successful values does not allocate. Error diagnostics are immutable shared owning values; borrowed primaryDiagnostic/diagnostics views remain conservatively valid only until their Status is destroyed or replaced.

Read-only empty diagnostic observation vector is owned by the common library and initialized before simulation commit phases. It is not a mutable alternate status source. Public query shapes are unchanged; all consumers must rebuild because the private shared-library value layout changed.

OBJECT standalone global-new probe verifies success creation/copy/move and selected Crowd commit after motion have zero allocations; actual one-shot prepare failure returns Result before mutation. Shared mode runs Result/Status and Crowd transaction contracts without pretending executable allocator interception covers DLL allocations.
entries.thread_affinity: Status is an owning value; concurrent mutation/replacement of one value is unsupported. Immutable diagnostic copies retain storage without callbacks.

trim.evidence: Current change rebuilds OBJECT composition, SHARED composition and core-only SHARED; runtime Result/Status and Crowd tests plus allocation probe are required. No higher module dependency.

cost_notes.why: Code and immutable storage ownership only; success allocates no diagnostics workspace. Error construction owns diagnostics and retains its existing construction cost.

entries.reason: Typed domain payloads share one deterministic binary envelope and digest contract instead of defining a second header in every domain.
entries.schema: eve.persistence.proto.BinarySnapshotEnvelope owns typed header fields, opaque domain payload wire bytes and a digest.
entries.version: The envelope carries the owning domain schema id and version; no independent envelope version is introduced.
entries.migration: The shared binary wire field numbers match the former transaction-specific envelope; legacy Value envelopes remain readable through domain compatibility readers.
entries.unknown_fields: The parser rejects unknown envelope fields and requires every stable header, nonempty payload bytes and a fixed-size digest.
entries.restore_atomicity: The parser verifies the complete digest before returning owned payload bytes; domain restore validates in a detached candidate before publication.

entries.reason: Foundation persistence modules can seal and verify typed Protobuf payload bytes with one binary interface.

trim.absent_profile: No L1-L4 trim claim is made for the common envelope.

entries.thread_affinity: The caller owns the payload; the injected hash provider controls callback behavior and must be safe for the caller thread.
cost_notes: Seal and verify cost linear time in payload bytes and two deterministic envelope serializations per operation.
